- When sentiment is consistently negative (last 3–5 days < -0.3), reduce forecasted price by 1–2% to avoid over-optimism.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike (e.g., >+5% from recent 5-day avg) and sentiment is neutral or positive, cap the forecast at 1–2% above recent peak to prevent overshoot.  
- If true outcome is significantly below forecast (e.g., >3% gap) and sentiment is negative, assume model overreacted — adjust downward by 1–3% for next period.  
- If forecast is consistently above true outcome over 3+ consecutive days, apply mean reversion: subtract 0.5–1.5% from forecast for next 3–5 days unless sentiment strongly supports.  
- If sentiment is positive but forecast is below true outcome, assume model is underweighting sentiment — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 2–3 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is below 10% of 30-day moving average, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overestimating momentum.  
- If sentiment is volatile (±0.3 or more in last 3 days), apply smoothing: forecast = 0.7×previous + 0.3×current sentiment-adjusted trend.
